summary: Phase 3 of the fleet map rework: an appliance's own box pin becomes the sole writer of where it lives, and the twin-tree rail gains the verbs to act on the tray instead of only describing it. Pinning a node's own marker on a plan (a placement with no camera) now sets ManagedNode.SiteId to that plan's site, and unpinning it clears SiteId again (ISiteService.AddPlacement/DeletePlacement, injected into INodeRegistry.UpdateNodeSite via a new SetNodeSiteBinder seam) - a camera placement never touches SiteId, since one recorder's cameras can sit in several places. This replaces PUT /api/nodes/{id}/building (removed) with the pin as the only writer, closing the gap the previous phase's rail rework left open. A new ManagedNode.NoFixedLocation flag lets an operator explicitly waive an appliance that genuinely has no place on any plan (a colo recorder, a hosted hub) - PUT /api/nodes/{id}/no-fixed-location, which also clears SiteId - so the fleet map's "not placed yet" tray can reach zero even for a fleet with an off-site box; a waived appliance stops counting as an outstanding one, and the tray root now shows two separate counters (cameras not on any plan, appliances whose own location is not pinned). In the tray, each unplaced camera row is now draggable onto a place or area row in the "Everywhere" tree (a row only highlights for a drag it can accept); dropping opens that place's editor already holding the camera and on the right area (BuildingEditorDialog's new initialPick/initialFloorId props). Every tray camera also gets an explicit "Place on a plan" button as the discoverable, non-drag path, and every tray node row gets a no-fixed-location toggle. Also swaps the hand-written browser-global allowlist in eslint.undef.config.mjs for the maintained `globals` package (now a real devDependency, package-lock updated) so `npm run lint:undef` keeps working without manually chasing new browser APIs.
compatibility: Backward compatible for existing installs. New column managed_node.no_fixed_location (BOOLEAN) is added by an idempotent, NULL-backfilling migration (20260908-01-node-no-fixed-location) and defaults to false for every existing node - nobody has made that decision yet, matching current behavior. Existing ManagedNode.SiteId assignments are unaffected and continue to colour a node's place exactly as before; the only behavior change is that the now-removed PUT /api/nodes/{id}/building route (already unreachable from any screen since the prior rail rework) is gone, and a fleet must use the box pin or the new no-fixed-location toggle going forward. No migration needed for existing placements or sites.
